naming_clarity.reason: Title and body use stakeholder vocabulary (fleet operator, insulation between pack and chassis, touch hazard, live part, applicable safety standard); the story mixes the words insulation and isolation for the same thing, but the plain insulation wording anchors the term so a non-implementer can still confirm it.

no_mechanism_leak.reason: Mostly implementation-free, but the out-of-scope sentence names the contactors, a hardware disconnect device that is an incidental design hint and not load-bearing for isolation monitoring.
no_mechanism_leak.suggestion: Say disconnecting the pack from the high-voltage circuit, as the cell-protection story does, or drop the clause; note that the cell-protection story and its requirements cover only cell voltage, cell temperature and pack-current faults, so the reaction to an isolation fault that this clause defers to them currently has no owner.

parent_fit.reason: Root of the V: the user_stories stage has no upstream stage (depends_on is empty) and the story has no outgoing trace link, so there is no parent to engage with and the axis is fully met by default.

single_user_capability.reason: Exactly one capability, watching the insulation between the high-voltage pack and the chassis and raising an isolation fault when it degrades below the minimum the applicable standard sets; cell protection and the contactor reaction are explicitly out of scope and one child requirement covers it.

user_observable.reason: Observable in principle (the pack raises an isolation fault), but the story names no observer, channel or bench check, so the fault reads as an internal state rather than a visible effect, and nothing says how anyone would establish that the barrier really fell below the minimum set by the standard.
user_observable.suggestion: Say where the fault is seen (for example a warning to the driver or a fault the workshop can read) and give a bench check: a known resistance connected between the high-voltage bus and the chassis makes the fault appear once it falls below the minimum set by the standard for the pack voltage, and not above it.

summary: One clean capability in plain language, but the observable names no channel or bench check for the isolation fault and the out-of-scope line names the contactors.
